A generated project says in its `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` which baseline it was generated on. To bring it
up to date, apply the upgrade steps of every release after that one, oldest first. Each step says how to tell
whether your project still needs it: run the **Needed when** command from the project root; exit status 0 means
the step applies. Steps that change the Gradle wrapper, `.github/` or `config/pmd/` touch files your `AGENTS.md`
leaves to a person: put them in a pull request of their own. **Required** steps keep the project building and
scanning clean on the new versions, **recommended** ones follow changed advice and **optional** ones adopt what new
projects get.

<a id="v0-1-b4"></a>

## Unreleased, on start.pyahu.io now

start.pyahu.io generates a monorepo: a platform of verticals in one Gradle build that keeps them apart, each with its own architecture, database, contract, image and deployment (ADR 0004). The monorepo guide is rewritten around it. A project with one service no longer lists the monorepo checklist items.

### Upgrade a project generated on v0.1-b3

<a id="v0-1-b4-checklist-without-monorepo"></a>

**1. A project with one service drops the monorepo checklist items** (optional)

- Files: `CHECKLIST.md`
- Needed when: `grep -q 'MONO-01' CHECKLIST.md`
- Check: `! grep -q 'MONO-' CHECKLIST.md`
- Why: [Monorepos with several services, step 1](/guides/monorepo/#mono-when)

The monorepo items (MONO-01 to MONO-13) now go only into generated monorepos. Delete the "Monorepos with
several services" section of `CHECKLIST.md`.

### Guide steps that changed

- [Monorepos with several services, step 2](/guides/monorepo/#mono-layout): A new step on the layout: one folder per vertical, `verticals/<name>/`, with its service in `service/` and its contract in `api/`, and room for its web app in `web/` (not generated yet); flat project names and an owner for every vertical.
- [Monorepos with several services, step 3](/guides/monorepo/#mono-boundaries-rule): The service convention plugin fails the build when a service depends on another service's project.
- [Monorepos with several services, step 4](/guides/monorepo/#mono-contracts): A contract lives in its service's `api` project, generated once and checked against `main` in CI.
- [Monorepos with several services, step 7](/guides/monorepo/#mono-fast-build): A new step on the configuration cache and a build cache that only builds of `main` save.
- [Monorepos with several services, step 8](/guides/monorepo/#mono-one-service): Each vertical has its own `AGENTS.md` and its service its own `compose.yaml`.
- [Monorepos with several services, step 9](/guides/monorepo/#mono-ci): One workflow builds every project with the cache of `main` and runs the convention plugins' tests.

### Other changes

- A monorepo option on start.pyahu.io and in the API (`layout=monorepo`, `verticals=name:architecture:database,...`), proven by fixtures/monorepo, which is what the generator produces for its options. Each vertical is a folder, `verticals/<name>/`, with its service in `service/` and its contract project in `api/`. Each vertical's `ArchitectureTest` names the packages it may use of the platform: itself, every contract and the libraries.
- The quality report keeps one report per project, so a build of several projects writes one for each service. A project with one service writes the same report as before.

<a id="v0-1-b3"></a>

## v0.1-b3, 2026-11-27

Spring Boot 4.2.0 with Spring Framework 7.1, Spring Security 7.2, Spring Data 2026.1, Micrometer 1.18 and OpenTelemetry 1.68, on Temurin 25.0.5.1 and Gradle 9.9.2. Projects generated on v0.1-b2 move their pins, the Gradle wrapper and one renamed property; a Next.js frontend also patches zstd in its runtime image. Projects generated before the quality gates can adopt them.

<a id="v0-1-b3-trivy-image"></a>

**2. Trivy 0.76.2 in CI** (required)

- Files: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Needed when: `grep -qF 'aquasec/trivy:0.76.0@' .github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Check: `! grep -qF 'aquasec/trivy:0.76.0@' .github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Why: [The container image and supply chain, step 7](/guides/container-image/#img-scanning)

The Trivy image is pinned in the workflow, not in the catalog. Replace it in every step that uses it:

```diff
-docker://aquasec/trivy:0.76.0@sha256:2416d1f74045b57274df1a340eee6b510cacd73c66a6ccb8da092b117eb7d222
+docker://aquasec/trivy:0.76.2@sha256:8f6bb947dbc528902e11f2f5be52f7b519f6a39d5d148f41166f2040499768fb
```

<a id="v0-1-b3-gradle-wrapper"></a>

**3. Gradle 9.9.2 in the wrapper** (required)

- Files: `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties`, `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar`, `gradlew`, `gradlew.bat`
- Needed when: `! grep -q 'gradle-9.9.2-bin.zip' gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties`
- Check: `./gradlew --version | grep -q 'Gradle 9.9.2'`
- Why: [Build and code quality, step 1](/guides/build-quality/#bld-wrapper)

Run the wrapper task twice: the first run writes the new version and checksum, the second runs on 9.9.2 and
writes its own wrapper jar and scripts.

```sh
./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version 9.9.2 \
  --gradle-distribution-sha256-sum 971fcd7150ca4ba04852c0b2ca0d2d0ab9468e14b03473eab19528809914c76b
./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version 9.9.2 \
  --gradle-distribution-sha256-sum 971fcd7150ca4ba04852c0b2ca0d2d0ab9468e14b03473eab19528809914c76b
```

<a id="v0-1-b3-forwarded-headers"></a>

**4. Rename the forwarded headers property** (required)

- Files: `src/main/resources/application.yaml`
- Needed when: `grep -q 'forward-headers-strategy' src/main/resources/application.yaml`
- Check: `./gradlew build`
- Why: [Security hardening, step 5](/guides/security/#sec-headers)

Spring Boot 4.2 deprecates `server.forward-headers-strategy`. Its `native` value is now `web-server`, and
setting both properties stops the application at startup.

```diff
 server:
-  forward-headers-strategy: native
+  request:
+    header:
+      forwarded:
+        strategy: web-server
```

Do the same in any profile file or Deployment environment variable that sets it
(`SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY` becomes `SERVER_REQUEST_HEADER_FORWARDED_STRATEGY`).

<a id="v0-1-b3-frontend-zstd"></a>

**5. Patch zstd in the frontend image** (required)

- Applies when: frontend is nextjs.
- Files: `frontends/web/Dockerfile`
- Needed when: `test -f frontends/web/Dockerfile && ! grep -q 'libzstd1=1.5.7+dfsg-1+deb13u1' frontends/web/Dockerfile`
- Check: `docker build --build-arg DEPLOYMENT_ID=check -t web-check frontends/web && docker run --rm --entrypoint dpkg-query web-check -W libzstd1 | grep -q deb13u1`
- Why: [The container image and supply chain, step 7](/guides/container-image/#img-scanning)

The Node base image still ships zstd 1.5.7+dfsg-1, which Trivy reports as HIGH (CVE-2026-124851), so the
image scan in CI fails. Install Debian's fixed package next to the zlib patch in the runtime stage, and keep
the zlib pin:

```diff
-    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends zlib1g=1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+deb13u1 \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends zlib1g=1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+deb13u1 libzstd1=1.5.7+dfsg-1+deb13u1 \
```

<a id="v0-1-b3-checklist-text"></a>

**6. Two checklist items changed their text** (recommended)

- Files: `CHECKLIST.md`
- Needed when: `grep -qE 'server.forward-headers-strategy pinned|otel-lgtm 0.37.0' CHECKLIST.md`
- Check: `! grep -qE 'server.forward-headers-strategy pinned|otel-lgtm 0.37.0' CHECKLIST.md`
- Why: [Security hardening, step 5](/guides/security/#sec-headers)

SEC-06 names `server.request.header.forwarded.strategy` instead of `server.forward-headers-strategy`, and
LOCAL-05 names `grafana/otel-lgtm` 0.41.1. Edit both lines and keep your ticks.

<a id="v0-1-b3-rabbitmq-starter"></a>

**7. The RabbitMQ starter is spring-boot-starter-rabbitmq** (required)

- Applies when: your build depends on spring-boot-starter-amqp to talk to RabbitMQ.
- Files: `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, `build.gradle.kts`
- Needed when: `grep -q 'spring-boot-starter-amqp' gradle/libs.versions.toml build.gradle.kts`
- Check: `./gradlew build`
- Why: [RabbitMQ, step 1](/guides/rabbitmq/#rmq-when)

In Spring Boot 4.2, `spring-boot-starter-amqp` is generic AMQP 1.0. Depend on `spring-boot-starter-rabbitmq`
for RabbitMQ's AMQP 0.9.1 client, and `spring-boot-starter-amqp-rabbitmq` only for RabbitMQ's AMQP 1.0
client. Auto-configuration classes moved from `org.springframework.boot.amqp` to
`org.springframework.boot.rabbitmq`; `spring.rabbitmq.*` properties are unchanged.

<a id="v0-1-b3-rest-template"></a>

**8. Plan the move off RestTemplate** (recommended)

- Applies when: your code uses RestTemplate, RestTemplateBuilder or TestRestTemplate.
- Files: `src/main/java`, `src/test/java`
- Needed when: `grep -rqE 'RestTemplate' src`
- Check: `./gradlew compileJava compileTestJava`
- Why: [HTTP clients and resilience, step 1](/guides/http-clients/#http-client-choice)

Spring Framework 7.1 deprecates `RestTemplate` for removal in 8.0 and Spring Boot 4.2 deprecates
`RestTemplateBuilder` and `TestRestTemplate`. The code keeps working with deprecation warnings. Move each
client to `RestClient` when you touch it, and tests to `RestTestClient` with `@AutoConfigureRestTestClient`.

<a id="v0-1-b3-quality-gates"></a>

**9. Adopt the quality gates and the quality report** (optional)

- Applies when: your project was generated before the quality gates and has no gradle/quality-report directory.
- Files: `build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle.kts`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, `gradle/quality-report/`, `config/pmd/ruleset.xml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `src/test/java`, `CHECKLIST.md`, `README.md`
- Needed when: `test ! -d gradle/quality-report`
- Check: `./gradlew check && jq -e '.status == "passed"' build/reports/pyahu/quality.json`
- Why: [CI pipelines, step 9](/guides/ci-pipelines/#ci-quality-report)

New projects fail the build on complex code (PMD), untested business rules (JaCoCo, 80% of lines and 70% of
branches in the domain and application packages), tests that notice no mistake (PIT, 70% of mutations) and
more architecture rules (ArchUnit), and write a quality report that CI requires to say passed. To adopt
them, generate the same project on [start.pyahu.io](https://start.pyahu.io) with the same name, group,
package and options into a temporary directory, then take from it what follows. The generator always serves
the newest release: if it is past v0.1-b3, you get the newer versions of these files, and the upgrade steps
of the later releases find that part done.

1. `gradle/quality-report/` and `config/pmd/ruleset.xml`, copied as they are.
2. `settings.gradle.kts`: `includeBuild("gradle/quality-report")` at the top of `pluginManagement`.
3. `gradle/libs.versions.toml`: the `pmd`, `jacoco`, `pitest`, `pitest-junit5` and `pitest-gradle-plugin`
   versions and the `pitest` plugin.
4. `build.gradle.kts`: the `jacoco`, `pmd`, `id("io.pyahu.quality-report")` and `alias(libs.plugins.pitest)`
   plugins; `check("RequireExplicitNullMarking", CheckSeverity.ERROR)` in the Error Prone options; and in
   place of your `tasks.test` block, everything from the comment "Fast tests on every change" to the end of
   `tasks.check`.
5. Tests: `@Tag("integration")` on every test that starts the application or a container
   (`ApplicationTest`, `DatabaseRolesTest` and `PendingMigrationsTest` in a generated project), the new
   project's `ArchitectureTest`, and its fast tests in `ping/application/` while the sample `ping` capability
   is still there. Your own domain and application code needs fast tests of its own.
6. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: in place of the step "Gradle build in the pinned JDK", every step from
   "Format" to "Keep the test and analysis reports".
7. `CHECKLIST.md`: the new items BLD-12, ARCH-11, TEST-10, TEST-11 and CI-15 and the new text of BLD-07;
   `README.md`: the paragraph about the quality report.

Existing code may fail the new gates. Fix the code or add tests; do not lower a limit.

<a id="v0-1-b3-agents-md"></a>

**10. Add AGENTS.md for coding agents** (optional)

- Applies when: your project was generated before AGENTS.md was added.
- Files: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`
- Needed when: `test ! -f AGENTS.md`
- Check: `test -f AGENTS.md && test -f CLAUDE.md`

New projects carry an `AGENTS.md` with what the build enforces, what to do when it fails and which guide to
read before each change, and a `CLAUDE.md` that points to it. Copy both from a project generated with the same
options and adjust the layout table if you moved packages.

<a id="v0-1-b3-release-notes-link"></a>

**11. Link these notes from README.md and AGENTS.md** (optional)

- Files: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`
- Needed when: `! grep -q 'initializer.pyahu.io/releases/' AGENTS.md`
- Check: `grep -q 'initializer.pyahu.io/releases/#v0-1-b3' AGENTS.md README.md`

New projects link to the release notes after their baseline. Add, after the Renovate sentence of
`README.md`:

```md
A new baseline also changes generated files: its
[release notes](https://initializer.pyahu.io/releases/#v0-1-b3) list, from this project's baseline on, each
step to apply and how to tell whether the project still needs it.
```

and, before "Leave these to a person" in `AGENTS.md`:

```md
## Upgrading to a newer baseline

The [release notes](https://initializer.pyahu.io/releases/#v0-1-b3) list every step after baseline v0.1-b3,
oldest first. Run a step's **Needed when** command from the repository root and apply the step only when it
exits 0, then run its **Check**. A step that changes a file listed below goes in its own pull request.
```

<a id="v0-1-b3-record-baseline"></a>

**12. Record v0.1-b3 as the project's baseline, last** (required)

- Files: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Needed when: `grep -qF 'baseline v0.1-b2' README.md AGENTS.md gradle/libs.versions.toml .github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Check: `! grep -qF 'v0.1-b2' README.md AGENTS.md gradle/libs.versions.toml .github/workflows/ci.yml`

Once every required step above that applies, and each other step you chose, passed its check, replace `v0.1-b2` with `v0.1-b3` and
`Spring Boot 4.1.2` with `Spring Boot 4.2.0` in these files. Until then the project still says v0.1-b2, so
whoever picks the upgrade up starts from these notes again.

### Guide steps that changed

- [Security hardening, step 5](/guides/security/#sec-headers): Pins `server.request.header.forwarded.strategy` (`web-server`), the Spring Boot 4.2 name.
- [HTTP clients and resilience, step 1](/guides/http-clients/#http-client-choice): RestTemplate is deprecated for removal; RestTemplateBuilder and TestRestTemplate with it.

### Other changes

- Release notes, on this page, in the Agent Skill and as GitHub releases; generated projects link to them.
- The Initializer itself runs on Spring Boot 4.2.0 and the same pins.
- The reference docs point at the Spring Boot 4.2, Spring Framework 7.1 and Spring Security 7.2 documentation.

<a id="v0-1-b2"></a>

## v0.1-b2

The first release with release notes. Its pins are kept in data/baselines/v0.1-b2.yaml so the next release can list what changed.
